goal: Define the product outcomes and observable acceptance for M07 package dependency governance from its approved Discovery, without selecting implementation details or authorizing SPEC/BUILD.

sources.location: Original 50-improvement task and explicit M07 approval for documentary PRD in this session
sources.license_notes: User scope and gate decision; no external content.

criteria.target: Every product goal, workflow, rule, requirement, metric, and acceptance criterion traces to the approved M07 Discovery or is explicitly marked as a proposed decision/open question.
criteria.evidence_method: Read the PRD and check its traceability table and source links against 0017, 0341, and 0342.
criteria.conditions: Document review only; no code or tests are authorized by this PRD stage.
criteria.validity_notes: Human approval of Discovery authorizes this PRD only.

criteria.target: The PRD specifies WHAT package maintainers and consumers must observe; it does not prescribe modules, algorithms, schema, file edits, command sequences, or build implementation.
criteria.evidence_method: Inspect every requirement and acceptance criterion for product-visible outcomes versus implementation instructions.
criteria.conditions: Any technical choice remains for SPEC.
criteria.validity_notes: Compatibility constraints may be stated as outcomes, not implementation design.

criteria.target: The PRD covers workspace dependency declarations, public package/export expectations, project build references, and prohibited direction only within an explicitly classified target boundary; it keeps production and test imports separate and makes the dirty-worktree baseline and legacy exceptions visible.
criteria.evidence_method: Compare scope, rules, exclusions, dependencies, risks, and open decisions with 0017 and 0342.
criteria.conditions: Do not classify a static discrepancy as a runtime/build failure or treat every workspace package as public.
criteria.validity_notes: The current inventory is worktree-specific and requires refresh before promotion.

criteria.source: Engineering Framework PRD Engine; 0341 M07 ready/evidence criterion
criteria.target: Requirements and acceptance criteria define measurable outcomes for dependency classification, declared direct dependencies, an explicit public-package set, target-graph direction, exceptions, and compatibility, while distinguishing documentary acceptance from later authorized build evidence.
criteria.evidence_method: Inspect requirement wording for actor, condition, observable result, scope, failure behavior, and evidence method; verify no unsupported numeric baseline or pass claim is introduced.
criteria.conditions: No tests/builds run at PRD stage.
criteria.validity_notes: Specific checks, slices, and tools are deferred to SPEC.

criteria.source: Original task safety constraints and 0342 P1-S1 scope
criteria.target: The PRD preserves local/synthetic scope, requires explicit approval/handoff for sensitive actions, keeps G21-5/G21-6 closed and production NO_GO, and grants no SPEC/BUILD/test or external authority.
criteria.evidence_method: Inspect goals, non-goals, permissions, failure behavior, risks, and next-gate wording against the user task and current gate record.
criteria.conditions: This human gate allows documentary PRD only.
criteria.license_notes: No real data or sensitive action.
criteria.validity_notes: Independent review does not replace the human PRD validation before SPEC.

criteria.source: 0017 M07 Discovery and approved P1-S1 gate decision
criteria.target: Unknown package-publicity rules, project-reference semantics, ownership of exceptions, and dirty-worktree freshness are recorded as risks or open decisions instead of silently fixed by the PRD.
criteria.evidence_method: Inspect risks, dependencies, open questions, metrics, and the next-gate section for named ownership or an explicit unresolved state.
criteria.conditions: No product or architecture decision may be inferred from package names or historical gates.
criteria.validity_notes: Open questions must be resolved in PRD validation or explicitly assigned to SPEC without changing product scope.
